content: Clear cell tumors belong to the surface epithelial-stromal tumor category of ovarian cancers and represent approximately 6% of these cases. These tumors can also occur in the pancreas and salivary glands. Benign and borderline forms of clear cell tumors are uncommon, with the majority of cases being malignant. Typically, these tumors present as cystic neoplasms that contain polypoid masses extending into the cystic cavity. On microscopic examination, the tumor cells are characterized by clear cytoplasm, which contains glycogen, and hobnail cells, which are cells that have secreted their glycogen. The architectural patterns of these tumors can vary and may include glandular, papillary, or solid arrangements.
